Title: Growth Marketing Manager – Paid Media & Klaviyo (AI-First)
Type: Full-time contractor
Seniority: Mid-level
Salary: USD 55,000–70,000/year + performance bonus
Location: Remote — Worldwide, excluding the United States, Canada, United Kingdom and Western Europe. Candidates must be available for at least four hours of overlap with Pacific Time.

About Nectar Life. We're a vertically integrated bath and body brand: handmade, vegan and cruelty-free. We make everything in our own 26,000 sq ft Las Vegas factory and sell it in our own stores on the Las Vegas Strip, Downtown Disney, Universal CityWalk and Waikiki, and online through Shopify.

The role. We're bringing growth in-house. You'll replace our paid-ads agency and own customer acquisition and retention end to end, reporting to the CEO. Your work will move sales visibly, and you'll help build our AI creative workflows from the ground up.

Must-haves (we screen for both first):

  • 3+ years of hands-on Meta Ads Manager work for ecommerce or DTC brands: you built, tested and scaled the campaigns yourself and can show spend, ROAS and CPA.

  • Hands-on Klaviyo: email and SMS flows, segmentation and campaigns you built, with revenue to show for them.

What you'll do:

  • Run Meta and TikTok ads: budgets, audiences, creative testing, scaling winners.

  • Run Klaviyo retention: welcome, abandoned cart, post-purchase and win-back flows, plus weekly sends.

  • Produce ad creative with AI tools (image, video, copy), then edit it to match our brand and keep product details accurate.

  • Report weekly on what worked, what didn't and what's next.

You'll stand out if you: have beauty, skincare, fragrance or gifting experience; edit short-form video; build automations with Claude, n8n or Make.

Hours: at least 4 hours overlap with 9am–5pm US Pacific.

Application questions:

  1. Upload a Meta Ads Manager screenshot of campaigns you ran (spend, purchases, ROAS visible).

  2. Upload a screenshot of a Klaviyo flow you built, with its revenue or conversion stats.

  3. Link one ad you made with AI tools and name the tools.

Who We Are:

Power Digital is an AI-Native Growth Firm built at the intersection of world-class talent and proprietary technology. We help leading and emerging brands grow by combining deep vertical expertise, strategic thinking, and enterprise intelligence to drive measurable business outcomes.

For more than a decade, we have built our business around one belief: the best technology makes great people better. Our teams of strategists, creatives, analysts, and technologists use Omega, our AI operating system, to surface opportunities faster, investigate what is driving performance, and execute approved work with greater speed and precision. Behind Omega is Iris, our proprietary intelligence layer, built on years of real performance data, strategic frameworks, testing, and learnings from across our client portfolio. AI expands the capacity of our people to think, create, solve harder problems, and make better decisions. Human judgment, creativity, and accountability remain central to how we work.

As a people-first firm, we value diversity in backgrounds and experiences. We strongly believe our people and culture are key to our success. We partner closely with our clients as an extension of their teams, working across strategy, execution, and measurement to identify what is truly blocking growth and determine what to do next. Our culture is built on people who are curious, ambitious, accountable, and committed to delivering meaningful results for our clients and for one another.

At Power Digital, we believe the future belongs to teams that combine the best talent with the best technology. We are building that future today.

***Proficiency in spoken and written English at an advanced level is required for this role.

***This job application is for a role at one of Power Digital's partner companies. Power Digital is assisting this partner company with its recruiting efforts. If you are selected for this position to interview, please make note of the above statement.

A day in the life:

As a Growth Marketing Manager, you’ll own the strategy and execution behind the integrated marketing campaigns that fuel Cardinal’s pipeline. You’ll architect full-funnel initiatives, from webinars and events to reports and eBooks, then lead cross-functional teams to bring each campaign to life with cohesive messaging and high-impact creative. Daily, you’ll monitor performance, optimize in real time, and ensure that every channel works together to generate high-quality leads. You’ll collaborate closely with internal contributors and contractors, keeping projects on track and jumping in to execute when needed. This is a role for someone who moves fast, thinks big, and owns outcomes end to end.

Responsibilities:

  • Campaign Strategy & Planning
  • Build full-funnel campaign strategies for major launches (webinars, in-person events, eBooks, reports).
  • Define audiences, messaging, channel mix, goals, and success metrics.
  • Develop campaign plans and timelines aligned with growth and revenue priorities.
  • Integrated Activation
  • Lead cross-channel execution across email, paid media, social, and web.
  • Create creative briefs and coordinate with design, copy, video, paid, and email teams.
  • Ensure campaigns land with cohesive messaging, strong creative, and clear CTAs.
  • Performance & Optimization
  • Monitor performance and identify what’s working, what’s not, and why.
  • Optimize live campaigns—messaging, audience, UX, offers, funnel flow.
  • Build testing plans and share insights to improve results continually.
  • Collaboration & Leadership
  • Manage internal contributors and contractors, ensuring deadlines and quality.
  • Step in to execute when needed—no ego, high ownership.
  • 12-Month Success Indicators
  • Launch 6–8 major campaigns that generate a measurable pipeline.
  • Improve conversion rates across key funnel stages.
  • Build a campaign playbook and reporting cadence.
  • Elevate the quality and cohesion of Cardinal’s thought leadership.

Role Requirements:

  • Data-driven, audience-obsessed growth marketer.
  • Comfortable owning both strategy and execution.
  • Strong communicator across creative and performance teams.
  • Obsessed with iteration—never settles for “good enough.”
  • Strong collaborator who gets the best from teammates and contractors.
  • Bias toward action and proactive problem-solving.
  • 5–7 years in B2B growth, demand gen, or integrated marketing (agency/professional services a plus).
  • Demonstrated success running multi-channel, full-funnel campaigns with measurable results.
  • Expertise in LinkedIn Ads, Meta Ads, Google Ads, email marketing platforms, and webinar tools.
  • Deep understanding of digital channels and how they work together.
  • Ability to write or refine campaign copy (emails, landing pages, ads).
  • Strong analytical skills: reporting, performance diagnosis, and conversion optimization.
  • Experience thriving in fast-paced environments with high standards.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, and backgrounds, who strive to make an impact inside and outside of the workplace. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employees' points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

VT Markets is an award-winning multi-asset brokerage trusted by over 3 million traders in over 160 countries with 500 employees—and growing. Founded in 2015 with the mission to make trading accessible to everyone, VT Markets offers a robust trading environment, over 1000 tradeable instruments, ultra-low spreads, and lightning-fast execution. We are committed to providing excellent customer service and empowering modern traders to seize market opportunities. Our platform allows traders to trade anytime, anywhere, supporting them in their journey to build a safe financial future.

Your Role in VT Markets
As the Growth Marketing, Partnership Business Lead within the Performance Marketing department, you will report directly to the Head of Performance Marketing and be based globally with coverage across international markets. In this executive role, you will serve as the primary commercial driver of VT Markets' global traffic supply chain—forging strategic partnerships with growth media networks, non-standard traffic sources, and agency partners. You will work closely with the Global Marketing COE, as well as internal Engineering and Data teams, to safeguard margin integrity, combat fraudulent traffic, and scale compliant, high-performance user acquisition pipelines.

Responsibilities

Global Supply Chain & Commercial Admission
  • Spearhead end-to-end commercial negotiations with global growth media networks, non-standard traffic networks, and core agency partners.
  • Own and enforce platform admission protocols to protect margin and interest across all traffic supply relationships.
  • Independently identify, develop, and onboard non-standard supply pipelines—including independent DSPs, ADXs, CTV publishers, and tier-1 Affiliate Networks.
Financial Audit & Traffic Integrity
  • Design and maintain a healthy, resilient traffic supply chain mechanism that upholds VT Markets' commercial standards.
  • Take full ownership of commercial reconciliations—including traffic mitigation, clawback execution, and recovery processes against fraudulent or non-compliant traffic sources.
  • Collaborate with Engineering and Data teams to audit raw vendor data logs and enforce data-driven accountability across supply partners.
Risk Control & Compliance Frameworks
  • Draft and implement large-scale user acquisition SLA risk-control frameworks, covering anti-hijacking protocols, click-injection filters, and strict clawback trigger thresholds.
  • Apply an adversarial negotiation mindset to proactively identify and close legal or contractual vulnerabilities with external partners.
  • Stay current on digital advertising fraud topologies and proactively evolve internal safeguards against emerging threats.

Requirements

What Success Looks Like
  • You have established a transparent, resilient global traffic supply chain with documented partner admission protocols—resulting in measurable reductions in fraudulent traffic and improved margin protection across all key supply relationships.
  • Your risk-control frameworks and SLA structures are consistently applied and credited with recovering significant value through successful clawback and reconciliation processes, demonstrating commercial discipline and legal acuity.
  • You are recognized by both internal stakeholders and external partners as a trusted authority in non-standard traffic development, having independently opened new supply pipelines that deliver compliant, scalable user acquisition for VT Markets.

What Makes You a Great Fit
Job Experience & Education
  • Bachelor's degree or above in Marketing, Business, Finance, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in overseas traffic business development or global media buying.
  • Prior experience in cross-border FinTech, digital trading platforms, or large-scale Web3 projects is highly advantageous.
Technical & Functional Skills
  • In-depth knowledge of the global long-tail traffic ecosystem; direct, established networks with independent DSPs, ADXs, CTV publishers, and tier-1 Affiliate Networks.
  • Proven ability to draft and enforce large-scale SLA risk-control frameworks including anti-hijacking, click-injection filters, and clawback trigger thresholds.
  • Highly analytical with the ability to collaborate with Engineering/Data teams to audit raw vendor data logs.
Soft Skills
  • Excellent negotiation skills with an adversarial mindset — able to hold firm commercial positions under pressure from external partners.
  • Strong understanding of digital advertising fraud topologies with a proactive, solutions-driven approach to risk mitigation.
  • Native or professional English fluency, capable of handling aggressive legal and commercial negotiations across cultures.
Other Requirements
  • This role involves frequent international travel and engagement across global time zones to manage partner relationships and supply chain operations.

Benefits

What Success Looks Like
  • You have established a transparent, resilient global traffic supply chain with documented partner admission protocols—resulting in measurable reductions in fraudulent traffic and improved margin protection across all key supply relationships.
  • Your risk-control frameworks and SLA structures are consistently applied and credited with recovering significant value through successful clawback and reconciliation processes, demonstrating commercial discipline and legal acuity.
  • You are recognized by both internal stakeholders and external partners as a trusted authority in non-standard traffic development, having independently opened new supply pipelines that deliver compliant, scalable user acquisition for VT Markets.

About The Role

We're looking for a strategist who can own growth across a pod of 5-8 clients in our direct response/info marketing division. You'll lead a cross-functional team - managing a media buyer, copywriter, and PM - and you'll be the person responsible for making sure every client has a real plan, real goals, and someone actively driving toward them.

This is the most senior client-facing role in the division and you are setting the strategic direction for each client's marketing - offer positioning, funnel strategy, creative direction, KPIs - and then leading your team to execute against it. When something's working, you know why; when something's not, you've already diagnosed the constraint and you're prescribing a fix, not waiting for the client to notice.

You're also a people manager. Your pod reports to you, which means setting priorities, running 1:1s, giving direct feedback, developing your people, and holding the standard on everything that leaves your pod. A strategist who does good strategy, but doesn't lead their team is only doing half of the job.

What Success Looks Like

  • Every client has documented goals broken down from quarterly to monthly to weekly, with specific KPIs - not vague targets or whatever the client said they wanted on the sales call
  • Your clients feel like someone is actively driving their growth, not maintaining what's already running and they trust you as an advisor
  • You lead client calls with a clear agenda, performance context, and recommendations which are prepared well before
  • When results are off, you can point to the specific constraint - not just "CPL is up." You know whether it's a creative fatigue issue, a funnel conversion problem, an offer misalignment, or a media buying execution gap, and you've already started working on it
  • Your team knows what they're working on and why it matters: they understand how their work connects to the client's goals
  • Your PM trusts you to push strategic initiatives proactively so they can build the plan. You're not making them guess what's next or chase you for direction
  • Team members on your pod are developing - they're getting real feedback, growing their skills, and they feel like they work for someone who's invested in them - not just someone who assigns work

A Day In This Role

Morning: You start the day reviewing performance across your accounts. Not deep analysis yet - a pulse check. Where's spend pacing? Any KPIs trending outside range? Any client messages that need your attention versus things your PM can handle? You walk into your pod standup knowing where each client stands and what the priorities are for the day so you can guide your team.

Throughout the day:

  • Lead or prep for client calls - clear agenda, updated performance narrative, strategic recommendations ready
  • Review team output: copy, creative briefs, funnel pages, ad concepts. You're checking that everything aligns with the strategy and meets the quality bar before it reaches the client
  • Push new strategic initiatives to your PM - a new funnel test, an offer restructure, a creative direction shift
  • Handle the judgment calls that require strategic thinking: a client pushing back on your recommendation, a media buyer flagging a performance anomaly, a copywriter unsure which direction to take on messaging

Meetings: You lead client calls while your PM captures action items and handles the follow-up, but you own the strategic conversation - performance narrative, recommendations, expectation management, the hard conversations when results aren't where they need to be.

Weekly rhythm: 1:1s with every direct report, priority sync with your PM, funnel mapping maintenance in Miro, and written client updates whether or not there's a call that week. You ensure reporting data is current and accurate - you don't necessarily pull every number, but you make sure the infrastructure is in place and the data is right.

Experience & Requirements

  • 5+ years in a marketing role - ideally in direct response, info/coaching, or performance marketing environments where you've owned client outcomes, not just deliverables
  • Demonstrated experience managing a team - this isn't your first time being responsible for other people's performance
  • Cross-discipline marketing competency: you don't need to be the best media buyer, copywriter, or funnel builder in the room, but you need to know what good looks like across all of them. You're directing and QA'ing work across paid media, copy, creative, funnels, and offers - you can't do that if you only understand one lane
  • Experience with offer strategy and positioning - pricing, packaging, and understanding what makes an offer convert in the info/coaching space
  • Clear written and verbal communication - you adapt how you communicate based on who you're talking to: strategic narrative for clients, clear direction for your team, concise context and recommendations for directors
  • Experience working in async-first environments
  • You use AI tools where they actually help - data analysis, research, consolidation - and you understand where they don't

You'll Do Well Here If

  • You think in terms of goals and constraints, not just campaigns and deliverables. "What is the client trying to achieve and what's actually in the way?" is how your brain works
  • You lead from the front - you set direction, make calls, and own the outcome
  • You're comfortable being wrong and adjusting - strategy is iterative. You set a plan, watch the data, and course correct when the numbers tell you to - you don't dig in on a bad plan because it was your idea
  • You're a people leader, not just a strategist with direct reports. Developing your team, giving real feedback, and building trust with the people who work for you matters to you
  • You push back when something doesn't make sense - with clients, with your team, with leadership. You do it with data and reasoning, not ego
  • You stay current on platforms, tools, and industry shifts
  • You're energized by the problem-solving side of this work - diagnosing why a funnel isn't converting, figuring out the right offer structure, identifying the one variable that's dragging performance

This Probably Isn't For You If

  • You see this role as account management with a strategy title. Keeping clients happy is part of the job, but if there's no plan and no measurable progress, the relationship doesn't matter
  • You default to reactive mode - waiting for problems to surface on client calls instead of catching them in the data first
  • You're not comfortable managing people - delegation is not the same as leadership
  • You avoid hard conversations - whether that's telling a client their expectations are unrealistic or telling a team member their work isn't at the standard
  • You rely on gut feel over data - the "I think this will work" answer, without being able to articulate your reasoning that is rooted in data and experience
  • You're looking for a role where you can specialize in one discipline: this role requires breadth across media, copy, creative, funnels, and offers
  • You treat AI as either a replacement for strategic thinking or something you can ignore entirely

About Plooto

Plooto is an all-in-one payment automation platform that helps businesses and accounting firms manage payables and receivables. More than 14,000 companies use Plooto to automate financial workflows, move money, and reconcile with their accounting systems.

We are building the financial operations platform small and medium-sized businesses can rely on to run with greater control, efficiency, and confidence.

The opportunity

Plooto is looking for a Director, Growth Marketing to own and scale our demand generation and customer growth engine.

Your primary mandate is to drive inbound pipeline for the sales team focused on our accounting firm channel, scale our direct self-serve motion efficiently, and build the cross-sell and upsell programs that grow customer LTV, while maintaining healthy CAC and payback. You will own growth strategy, marketing-sourced demand, direct and self-serve acquisition, lifecycle and customer growth, and the instrumentation and economics beneath the funnel, partnering closely with Sales on pipeline quality and conversion. You will report to the Head of Marketing.

This is a high-volume, low-ACV SMB business. Success requires sharp judgment about where paid acquisition, self-service, and sales assistance each earn their place, and the discipline to grow efficiently rather than simply spend into growth.

This is a player-coach role. You will set strategy and own the numbers, and you will stay hands-on in the funnel model, the channel mix, and experimentation. The person in this role will start with a small team and will use systems, automation, and AI to scale ouput.

We are looking for a builder. You will have personally stood up a demand or growth engine from an immature starting point, owned a pipeline number and its efficiency, and used modern tooling and AI to scale programs.

What you will do

  • Own the demand engine for our accounting firm channel. Build the strategy and channel mix that feeds the channel sales team inbound pipeline that actually converts, not just top-of-funnel volume.
  • Scale the direct and self-serve motion efficiently. Grow acquisition through the direct and product-led funnel while protecting CAC and payback.
  • Own growth economics. Set and be accountable for the demand waterfall, CAC, payback, funnel conversion, and growth by motion. Partner with Finance, Payments Strategy, and Sales on the models, while being comfortable getting into the weeds yourself.
  • Grow customer LTV. Build the cross-sell, upsell, and lifecycle programs that increase ARPU and expansion within our existing base.
  • Set multi-channel demand strategy. Decide where the next marginal dollar goes across paid, SEM/SEO/AEO, lifecycle and nurture, webinars, and content-driven inbound.
  • Own the website as a growth asset. Treat as a core conversion surface, running a continuous CRO program of testing, iteration, and personalization across landing pages, signup, and key conversion paths to lift conversion and marketing-sourced pipeline.
  • Build the growth systems. Partner with MarketingOps and RevOps to mature our attribution, reporting, and a disciplined experimentation cadence that enables fast learning loops.
  • Use AI as a force multiplier. Build an AI operating infrastructure via agents, prompts, and workflows that strategically scale content, research, analysis, and reporting, thoughtfully deploying human intelligence and domain expertise to train and guide the outputs.
  • Partner across the business. Work with Sales, Product, Data, and Finance to remove constraints across the customer journey and drive accountability through collaboration (without needing every function to report to you).
  • Lead and grow a lean team. Direct a small team and partner with senior leadership to scale as we grow.

What success looks like

In your first six months, you will have:

  • Set a clear growth strategy across the accounting channel, direct, and self-serve motions, with explicit choices about where to invest and why.
  • Grown marketing-sourced pipeline for the channel sales team, with measurable improvement in lead quality and conversion.
  • Instrumented the funnel end-to-end and established a single, trusted view of CAC, payback, and conversion by motion.
  • Improved acquisition efficiency while growing volume, moving CAC payback in the right direction.
  • Launched a cross-sell, upsell, or lifecycle program that measurably lifts ARPU or expansion revenue.
  • Established a disciplined experimentation cadence that produces real, repeatable wins.
  • Built meaningful leverage through automation and AI, raising output without proportional headcount.
  • Directed your team against clear priorities, leveraging strengths and empowering them to hit their metrics

What you bring

  • Proven experience building a demand or growth engine from an immature base. You can point to the systems, funnel, and motion you created rather than primarily inherited.
  • Personally quantitative. You own CAC, payback, and a funnel model without leaning on an analyst, and you reason clearly about cohort vs. in-period conversion, channel efficiency, and where the next marginal dollar earns its return.
  • Real experience in low-ACV, high-volume SMB growth, not an enterprise or ABM-only background.
  • Experience generating demand for a sales-led motion, ideally one fed through a channel, partner, or other intermediary (like a franchise or agency).
  • Fluency across both sales-fed demand generation and self-serve / product-led growth.
  • Hands-on multi-channel craft across paid, SEM/SEO/AEO, lifecycle and nurture, webinars, and content-driven inbound.
  • Hands-on experience owning a website and a structured CRO/experimentation program, ideally on a self-serve or PLG funnel.
  • Experience owning both customer acquisition and expansion / ARPU programs.
  • AI fluency and strategic POV. You use AI daily, with real leverage to show for it, and you have a clear point of view on where it creates value and where it adds noise.
  • A hands-on operating style suited to a lean team at Plooto's scale.
  • Executive-caliber collaboration with Sales, Product, Data, and Finance.
  • Canadian market knowledge and a base in Canada.

Strongly preferred

Experience marketing to or through accountants, bookkeepers, tax professionals, or the accounting-software ecosystem, or other trusted SMB intermediaries such as advisor networks, resellers, or franchises. Experience in SMB fintech, payments, payroll, practice management, or vertical SaaS; blended PLG and sales-assisted motions.

Why Become a Plootonian?

If you're looking to make a meaningful impact, look no further. We're transforming the payments space in North America by delivering an unrivalled product experience that solves a real and pressing problem for SMBs.

One of the biggest challenges small businesses face is managing their finances and cash flow—and Plooto helps address that. We have strong product-market fit, a significant opportunity ahead, and the backing of experienced fintech leaders.

You'll join a team that cares deeply about customer impact, takes pride in its craft, and moves with urgency. We're just getting started, and you'll help shape the next chapter of our growth story.

Join Plooto and be part of a mission that matters.

Our Commitment to Inclusion

Plooto is committed to building an inclusive workplace where people of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives can thrive. We know great teams are built through diverse thinking, and we encourage you to apply even if your experience does not align perfectly with every qualification listed.

Accommodation is available throughout the recruitment process in accordance with applicable accessibility legislation. If you require accommodation at any stage, please let us know—we're happy to work with you.

What You Can Expect

Zoom is hiring five dedicated PLG (Product-Led Growth) Marketing Leads to own organic growth for five of its highest-priority AI products — each role reporting directly into the CEO org.


This is an individual contributor role at the intersection of product marketing, organic growth, and AI-native content creation. You'll shape how users discover and adopt Zoom's productivity products—from product insight through content creation, distribution, and measurement. This is an organic-only role—there is no paid activation budget. All growth will be driven through content, SEO/AEO, social, and conversion optimization.


About the Team

The Zoom productivity team is building a new AI-native way to work—helping users move faster from conversation and ideation to polished, editable deliverables. As the product grows, this role will help more users understand its value and adopt it in their daily work. We're a product-led team looking for someone with sharp product judgment, hands-on content execution, and a genuine understanding of how people work and what earns their attention.


Responsibilities — Focus: Acquisition & Sign-up

  • Develop deep working knowledge of Zoom's productivity products: who uses them, what problems they solve, how they compare to alternatives, and where their real advantages lie.
  • Translate product positioning and messaging for PLG audiences that starts with the user problem, not the feature list—translating product capabilities into clear, outcome-oriented value.
  • Own end-to-end content creation and publication—including demos, tutorials, comparisons, social posts, emails, and web copy—from concept through measurement.
  • Use AI tools across the full content workflow—research, scripting, demo creation, editing, and iteration—to move quickly without sacrificing quality.
  • Own the acquisition and sign-up funnel: build a repeatable content and distribution engine to drive organic discovery, landing page conversion, and sign-up completion.
  • Optimize landing pages, signup flows, and run CRO experiments to improve conversion rates.
  • Execute SEO and AEO content to improve organic discoverability and drive qualified traffic.
  • Create and distribute platform-native content across X, YouTube, LinkedIn, Reddit, TikTok, and Instagram Reels—matching format and depth to each platform's audience while maintaining Zoom brand guidelines.
  • Track what's working using engagement, trial, subscription, and adoption signals—then use those findings to improve content and calls to action.
  • Partner with Online Marketing on email campaigns and in-product activation—ensuring messaging consistency and coordinated user journeys.
  • Partner with product managers, designers, engineers, and marketing teams to keep product stories accurate and moving at the pace of product development.

What We're Looking For

  • 8+ years PLG experience in product marketing, content marketing, growth marketing, or social content, with focus on digital products (SaaS, AI tools, productivity platforms, or creator products).
  • Strong product instincts: ability to identify the most important user problems, recognize genuine differentiators, and turn those into product stories that are simple, specific, and credible.
  • Practical fluency using AI tools for research, scripting, demo creation, video editing, and content iteration—demonstrated through shipped work, not just familiarity.
  • Demonstrated ability to personally create and publish end-to-end work: product videos, screen-recorded demos, and social content for digital products.
  • Strong understanding of how audiences, content formats, and distribution differ across TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube, X, Reddit, and LinkedIn—with demonstrated depth on multiple platforms.
  • Track record of building from scratch: cold-starting a content channel, product launch, or distribution system and driving it forward through ambiguity (candidates who have built and grown their own content channels with measurable results are encouraged to apply).
  • Comfort with rapid experimentation and scrappy execution: a willingness to test unconventional approaches, learn from what doesn't work, and iterate quickly without needing perfect conditions or established playbooks.
  • Experience at an AI-native, SaaS, productivity, or creator-product company is preferred—though not required if the work demonstrates the right instincts and execution ability.
